manifest.title: WeaveSignal
manifest.author: The WeaveSignal contributors
manifest.tagline: An internet radio and video studio: a live room with callers, the desk, playout, streams and chat
manifest.description:
<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 The WeaveSignal contributors -->
WeaveSignal is talk-radio software: presenters, guests and callers meet in a live room, a desk
mixes the programme with a mix-minus for each person, and playout sends it to listeners.

This package runs release one's server in one app: the control plane (Rust, Axum), the live
chat (Rust, Axum), the desk (Rust, GStreamer), Liquidsoap 2.5 for playout and for the listener
process that holds the stream with `icecast.server`, LiveKit with its own TURN, and the
station's public pages. It uses Cloudron's PostgreSQL and mail.

The studio app for presenters and screeners (Linux and Windows) connects to it over https.
Documentation: https://weavesignal.top. Source: https://forgejo.weavesignal.top/WeaveSignal/weavesignal.

LISTENERS_DOMAIN.title: Listener stream
LISTENERS_DOMAIN.description: The listener stream (Ogg Opus), served by icecast.server behind this domain. It is not listed in any directory.

ROOM_DOMAIN.title: Live room signalling
ROOM_DOMAIN.description: LiveKit's signalling for presenters, guests and callers (WebSocket). Room access needs a short-lived token from the station.

PUBLIC_DOMAIN.title: Public pages
PUBLIC_DOMAIN.description: The station's public pages, outside Cloudron's login: the player with call-in and the live chat, invited guests' join page, the echo test, podcast feeds, show cards and episode files. The app's own domain stays for the studio.

LIVEKIT_MEDIA_PORT.title: Live room media (UDP)
LIVEKIT_MEDIA_PORT.description: LiveKit's one WebRTC media port (ADR-0023). Default 7882; a port in 52000-60000 or 443/udp are alternatives, and any free UDP port may be used. Avoid 50000-51000, Cloudron's own TURN relay range.

TURN_UDP_PORT.title: TURN over UDP
TURN_UDP_PORT.description: LiveKit's built-in TURN over UDP. Off by default: guests who cannot use the media port use TURN over TLS. Cloudron's own TURN holds 3478, so 3479 or 13478; any free UDP port may be used.

TURN_TLS_PORT.title: TURN over TLS
TURN_TLS_PORT.description: LiveKit's built-in TURN over TLS, for guests on networks that block UDP and for GrapheneOS's browser (ADR-0059). On Cloudron the default is 15349, because Cloudron's own TURN holds 5349 (ADR-0106); any free TCP port may be used.

LIVEKIT_TCP_PORT.title: Live room media over TCP
LIVEKIT_TCP_PORT.description: LiveKit's ICE over TCP, a fallback when UDP is blocked. Off by default: TURN over TLS covers the same guests. Default 7881; any free TCP port may be used.

manifest.postInstallMessage:
<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 The WeaveSignal contributors -->
Your station is installed. The guide is at https://weavesignal.top/docs/how-to/install-on-cloudron/.

* The station's settings are in `/app/data/weavesignal.env`, and its generated secrets (the
  station identifier, LiveKit's key, the control plane's admin token, the listener password,
  and the keys that hash chatters' and staff's email addresses) are in `/app/data/secrets.env`.
  Keep the email keys: a new one finds none of the accounts made before. Open them with the File Manager; restart the app after an edit.
* The listener stream is at `https://<listener domain>/programme.opus`. It is in no directory
  and open to anyone with the address; set `LISTENERS_AUTH=on` in `weavesignal.env` to ask for
  the user `listener` and `LISTENERS_PASSWORD` from `secrets.env`.
* The player page, with call-in and the live chat, is at `https://<public domain>/`; podcast
  feeds, show cards and episode files are served there too. The chat's sign-in codes are sent
  through Cloudron's mail (`MAIL_MODE` in `weavesignal.env`).
* Staff: in the studio app, choose **Use the station key instead** with `CONTROL_ADMIN_TOKEN`,
  add yourself as an admin under **Settings → Staff**, then sign in as yourself. Each member
  of staff then gets their own account there.
* Room tokens: `POST /api/v1/room/tokens` with a staff sign-in or `CONTROL_ADMIN_TOKEN` as the bearer.
* The public ports (room media over UDP, TURN over TLS, and the optional TURN over UDP and ICE
  over TCP) must be open in the server's firewall and any cloud firewall.
<sso>
* The station's own domain is behind Cloudron's login; the listener, room and public domains
  are not, and are protected by the listener password, by room tokens, and by serving only
  the public routes.
</sso>
manifest.changelog:
- **WeaveSignal, release one**, the first public version (app id `top.weavesignal.cloudronapp`).
- **The listener stream is open by default** (`LISTENERS_AUTH=off`), unlisted, as in the Compose bundle; set it to `on` to ask for a password.
- **A caller's return is no longer choppy**: the desk stamps each output block from its place in the mix, not from the clock when it is encoded (0.0 % concealed, from 30–50 %).
- The edge passes only its own `Cache-Control`; the unused `hls_origin` port is retired.
